chapter: Youth, the road and arrival in California
title: The school dance orchestra and getting kicked out for smoking
summary: He led the Bordentown dance orchestra, wanted to play jazz, and explains the demerit system that ended Dizzy's time at the school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: They had a dance orchestra in school. They had a band and a dance orchestra. And the dance orchestra fell to me, I guess, because I was... There was more than one bass player, mostly tuba players, but I guess I was the one that aspired to Jazz more than the rest of them. The other
guys... I started out to be a legitimate musician, too -- and I'll get to that later.
In these school bands...did Dizzy or Charlie Shavers play in the same bands you did?
Briefly. Briefly. But they were there such a short while... I was probably there longer than they were.
What did Dizzy get kicked out for?

Who, Diz? I don't know what Diz did. But at that time you could get kicked out of school for smoking. And I got caught smoking once, and I got one demerit, and it just took three demerits to get kicked out. It was a real ROTC.
